The western side of this ledge protrudes to the right. The view is to the south-east, and the dirt road to Feshkha, where a building can be seen. Compare with Humbert and Chambon 1994: Fig. 427.

caption_or_note: (L. Boer, 21 March 1954) The photograph is taken in L.94, with the reinforcement wall of L.90 (the back of L.89) on the right. The view is looking north over L.92, L.88 and L.81, towards the tower. In 1992 this has vanished.

title: Photograph 39: Roland de Vaux, accompanied by two students of the Ecole Biblique, is surveying at L.96.
caption_or_note: (L. Boer, 25 March 1954) Roland de Vaux, accompanied by two students of the Ecole Biblique, is surveying at L.96. Number 96 can be read on the light coloured rock on the left of de Vaux’s instrument. The men are standing next to the cistern (L.91) that was being excavated that week. Behind the cistern, the tents, the Dead Sea, and the mountains of TransJordan are visible.
